question: How does Simon Peter identify himself in the opening of his second epistle, and to whom is it addressed?
opt1: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained like precious faith with us through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
opt2: Simon Peter, a bishop of the church of Antioch, to all converted proselytes dwelling in Alexandria
opt3: Simon Peter, an elder of the circumcision, to the dispersed tribes keeping the ceremonial ordinances of Moses
opt4: Simon Peter, a prisoner of the Lord in Rome, to the governors and rulers of the provinces of Galatia
correct: Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained like precious faith with us through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
explanation: Peter introduces himself as both servant and apostle, addressing believers who share an equally precious faith grounded in the imputed righteousness of God and our Savior Jesus Christ. 2 Peter 1:1 (KJV) - "Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained like precious faith with us through the righteousness of God and our Saviour Jesus Christ:"

question: According to 2 Peter 1:3-4, what has God's divine power bestowed upon believers through exceeding great and precious promises?
opt1: That by these ye might acquire earthly sovereignty and political immunity from Roman persecution
opt2: That by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust
opt3: That by these ye might construct a physical temple in Jerusalem surpassing Solomon's splendor
opt4: That by these ye might attain angelic immortality without experiencing physical death or trial
correct: That by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust
explanation: Through His divine power, God supplies all things essential for life and godliness, granting magnificent promises enabling believers to share in the divine nature while escaping worldly corruption. 2 Peter 1:3-4 (KJV) - "According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us to glory and virtue: Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust."

question: In the sacred progression of Christian virtues outlined in 2 Peter 1:5-7, what full sequence of qualities are believers exhorted to add with all diligence to their faith?
opt1: Add to your faith fasting; and to fasting tithes; and to tithes ritual washings; and to washings sabbaths; and to sabbaths phylacteries
opt2: Add to your faith rhetoric; and to rhetoric philosophy; and to philosophy civic office; and to civic office wealth; and to wealth fame
opt3: Add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; and to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; and to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity
opt4: Add to your faith visions; and to visions prophecies; and to prophecies miracles; and to miracles authority; and to authority dominion
correct: Add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; and to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; and to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity
explanation: Peter delineates seven vital spiritual virtues to be diligently developed upon the foundation of faith, culminating in sacrificial agape love. 2 Peter 1:5-7 (KJV) - "And beside this, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge; And to knowledge temperance; and to temperance patience; and to patience godliness; And to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity."

question: How does Peter describe the spiritual condition of a professing believer who lacks these essential virtues of spiritual growth?
opt1: He that lacketh these things has never heard the oral proclamation of the gospel message
opt2: He that lacketh these things is automatically condemned without any possibility of restoration
opt3: He that lacketh these things has merely failed in intellectual philosophical comprehension
opt4: He that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins
correct: He that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins
explanation: A Christian who fails to cultivate these spiritual graces suffers from spiritual shortsightedness and blindness, losing sight of the purifying forgiveness received at conversion. 2 Peter 1:9 (KJV) - "But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off, and hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins."

question: What earnest exhortation and enduring reward does Peter present regarding confirming one's calling and election?
opt1: Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall: for so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom
opt2: Wherefore seek after signs and wonders from heaven, that an earthly kingdom may be established before all nations
opt3: Wherefore withdraw into uninhabited wilderness caverns, that an angelic escort may preserve your mortal flesh
opt4: Wherefore observe all new moons and ceremonial festivals, that a Levitical blessing may be granted unto your children
correct: Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall: for so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom
explanation: Believers are urged to demonstrate the reality of their election through fruitful godly living, which ensures spiritual perseverance and a triumphant entrance into Christ's eternal kingdom. 2 Peter 1:10-11 (KJV) - "Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall: For so an entrance shall be ministered unto you abundantly into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ."

question: Why does Peter deem it urgent to continually remind believers of these foundational truths while he remains in his earthly body?
opt1: Knowing that a major schism has already dissolved the churches of Asia Minor
opt2: Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me
opt3: Knowing that the Roman emperor has issued an edict banishing all apostles from the capital
opt4: Knowing that his written epistles would be lost unless repeatedly transcribed by scribes
correct: Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me
explanation: Aware of his imminent departure from this life as foretold by the Lord Jesus Christ, Peter faithfully stirred up the believers to remember sound doctrine after his decease. 2 Peter 1:13-14 (KJV) - "Yea, I think it meet, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance; Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me."

question: On what historic eyewitness reality does Peter refute the accusation that the apostles followed cunningly devised fables?
opt1: Found ancient mythological scrolls preserved in the catacombs of the city of Rome
opt2: Received secret mystical knowledge from angelic messengers during nocturnal dreams
opt3: Were eyewitnesses of his majesty, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased
opt4: Consulted the philosophical archives of Alexandria and Athens regarding divine emanations
correct: Were eyewitnesses of his majesty, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased
explanation: The apostolic proclamation of Christ's glory and coming rests not on fabricated myths, but on Peter, James, and John's firsthand eyewitness experience of the Transfiguration on the holy mountain. 2 Peter 1:16-18 (KJV) - "For we have not followed cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but were eyewitnesses of his majesty. For he received from God the Father honour and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the excellent glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. And this voice which came from heaven we heard, when we were with him in the holy mount."

question: How does Peter describe the more sure word of prophecy, and to what does he compare its illuminating role?
opt1: As an obscure riddle sealed away from human comprehension until the end of time
opt2: As a transient candle that flickers and extinguishes under the slightest wind of controversy
opt3: As an outdated system of legal shadows that has lost all spiritual relevance for believers
opt4: As unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts
correct: As unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts
explanation: Scriptural prophecy is confirmed as thoroughly dependable, serving as a guiding lamp shining in spiritual darkness until the dawn of Christ's return and inner illumination. 2 Peter 1:19 (KJV) - "We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:"

question: What primary theological principle does Peter establish regarding the origin and exposition of prophetic Scripture?
opt1: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation
opt2: Knowing this first, that prophetic writings may be reinterpreted according to secular political shifts
opt3: Knowing this first, that ancient prophecies applied exclusively to the generation that wrote them
opt4: Knowing this first, that prophetic texts require allegorical modification by synagogue elders
correct: Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation
explanation: Prophecy does not originate from human insight or individual ingenuity, and therefore cannot be interpreted according to isolated, subjective human fancy. 2 Peter 1:20 (KJV) - "Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation."

question: How was Scripture produced in ancient times according to the inspired declaration in 2 Peter 1:21?
opt1: Prophecy came through philosophical consensus debated in the academic forums of Greece
opt2: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost
opt3: Prophecy came by royal decrees commissioned by the monarchs of Judah and Israel
opt4: Prophecy came through poetic imagination cultivated during prolonged periods of solitary isolation
correct: For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost
explanation: Biblical prophecy did not stem from human volition; rather, consecrated instruments of God spoke divine truth under the direct guidance and inspiration of the Holy Spirit. 2 Peter 1:21 (KJV) - "For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost."

question: What insidious strategy will false teachers employ within the church, and what catastrophic consequence do they bring upon themselves?
opt1: Openly demand violent revolution against Roman governors, bringing imperial military retaliation
opt2: Insist upon returning to Levitical animal sacrifices in Jerusalem, bringing temple excommunication
opt3: Privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction
opt4: Refuse to engage in commerce or agriculture, bringing severe physical poverty upon their followers
correct: Privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction
explanation: Just as false prophets plagued ancient Israel, deceptive teachers secretly infiltrate the church with destructive heresies, renouncing the Master who redeemed them and courting swift judgment. 2 Peter 2:1 (KJV) - "But there were false prophets also among the people, even as there shall be false teachers among you, who privily shall bring in damnable heresies, even denying the Lord that bought them, and bring upon themselves swift destruction."

question: What historical example of divine judgment against celestial beings does Peter cite in 2 Peter 2:4?
opt1: God stripped the cherubim of their wings and banished them to wander across the desolate desert
opt2: God pardoned the rebellious angels after a season of penitence and restored them to their heavenly thrones
opt3: God transformed the fallen angels into mortal men so they might seek salvation through earthly repentance
opt4: God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment
correct: God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment
explanation: God's uncompromising justice was demonstrated when He cast rebellious angels into Tartarus, binding them in chains of gloomy darkness until the final day of judgment. 2 Peter 2:4 (KJV) - "For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;"

question: How did God demonstrate both unyielding judgment and sovereign deliverance during the antediluvian flood?
opt1: Spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly
opt2: Spared the cities of the plains while submerging the mountain peaks with torrents of fire
opt3: Delivered seventy elders from the floodwaters through angelic chariots of fire
opt4: Granted the antediluvian civilization another thousand years of probation before sending rain
correct: Spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly
explanation: God wiped away an ungodly ancient civilization with a global deluge, yet faithfully delivered Noah, who proclaimed divine righteousness, along with seven members of his household. 2 Peter 2:5 (KJV) - "And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;"

question: How did God execute judgment on Sodom and Gomorrha, and what was the ongoing experience of righteous Lot dwelling among them?
opt1: Sending a drought upon Sodom and Gomorrha, while Lot accumulated great wealth from trade
opt2: Turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, and delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked
opt3: Exiling the inhabitants of Sodom to Babylon, while Lot served as prime minister of the cities
opt4: Destroying Sodom with pestilence, while Lot celebrated joyful feasts with pagan neighbors
correct: Turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, and delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked
explanation: Sodom and Gomorrha were reduced to ashes as an enduring warning to the ungodly, while righteous Lot was rescued, having suffered daily anguish over the immoral behavior of his neighbors. 2 Peter 2:6-8 (KJV) - "And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)"

question: What overarching theological truth does Peter establish from these historical demonstrations of divine wrath and mercy?
opt1: The Lord delays all retributive justice until earthly governments establish righteous legal codes
opt2: The Lord treats the righteous and the wicked with identical temporal prosperity and ease
opt3: The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished
opt4: The Lord overlooks moral transgression whenever offenders offer costly monetary sacrifices
correct: The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished
explanation: God's past interventions prove His sovereign capability both to rescue the faithful from trials and to keep the unrighteous under restraint until the day of final reckoning. 2 Peter 2:9 (KJV) - "The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:"

question: How does Peter contrast the reckless arrogance of false teachers who despise authority with the behavior of holy angels?
opt1: Whereas angels openly rebuke human magistrates in public city assemblies
opt2: Whereas angels execute instant destruction upon secular kings who reject the truth
opt3: Whereas angels refuse to acknowledge the supreme judicial authority of the Lord
opt4: Whereas angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord
correct: Whereas angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord
explanation: While presumptuous, self-willed apostates insolently blaspheme dignities and heavenly realities, even mighty holy angels do not utter reviling accusations before God. 2 Peter 2:10-11 (KJV) - "Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities. Whereas angels, which are greater in power and might, bring not railing accusation against them before the Lord."

question: Whose covetous path do these apostate teachers pursue, and how was that greedy prophet miraculously rebuked?
opt1: Following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; but was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet
opt2: Following the way of Gehazi the servant of Elisha, who was rebuked by sudden leprosy
opt3: Following the way of Korah the Levite, who was swallowed up alive by the earth
opt4: Following the way of King Jeroboam, whose hand withered as he reached out against the altar
correct: Following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; but was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet
explanation: Corrupt teachers walk in the footsteps of Balaam, motivated by financial greed, whose irrational madness was restrained when a speechless donkey spoke with a human voice. 2 Peter 2:15-16 (KJV) - "Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness; But was rebuked for his iniquity: the dumb ass speaking with man's voice forbad the madness of the prophet."

question: With what vivid metaphors does Peter characterize these deceptive teachers, and what false promise do they make while living as slaves of vice?
opt1: These are fertile vineyards yielding sweet grapes; while they promise austerity, they indulge in riches
opt2: These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; while they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption
opt3: These are steadfast anchors holding ships in storms; while they promise peace, they ignite armed revolts
opt4: These are glowing beacons guiding wanderers at sea; while they promise guidance, they lead into solitude
correct: These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; while they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption
explanation: False teachers offer empty spiritual promises like dried-up springs and storm-tossed clouds, offering spurious moral freedom while remaining enslaved to their own depravity. 2 Peter 2:17-19 (KJV) - "These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest; to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever. For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh, through much wantonness, those that were clean escaped from them who live in error. While they promise them liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption: for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he brought in bondage."

question: What grave warning does Peter issue regarding individuals who have escaped worldly pollutions through Christ but are entangled again and overcome?
opt1: Their spiritual condition remains entirely neutral without any increase in accountability
opt2: They will instantly regain all spiritual rewards whenever they attend an annual festival
opt3: The latter end is worse with them than the beginning, for it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness
opt4: Their temporal sins will be excused because of the theological ignorance of their ancestors
correct: The latter end is worse with them than the beginning, for it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness
explanation: Apostasy is disastrous; turning away after possessing knowledge of the truth produces a hardened condition far more tragic and culpable than initial pagan ignorance. 2 Peter 2:20-21 (KJV) - "For if after they have escaped the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein, and overcome, the latter end is worse with them than the beginning. For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after they have known it, to turn from the holy commandment delivered unto them."

question: What two graphic proverbs does Peter cite in 2 Peter 2:22 to depict the wretched relapse of apostates to their unclean nature?
opt1: The eagle returns to its solitary mountain crag; and the lion to its predatory den
opt2: The ox returns to its wooden yoke; and the sheep to the barren pastures of the desert
opt3: The serpent returns to its rocky crevice; and the moth to the consuming flame
opt4: The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire
correct: The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire
explanation: Peter employs visceral proverbial imagery from Proverbs 26:11 to show that apostates, despite temporary external reformation, remain unchanged in inner nature, returning inevitably to filth. 2 Peter 2:22 (KJV) - "But it is happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog is turned to his own vomit again; and the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire."

question: What primary purpose does Peter articulate for writing both of his epistles to the beloved saints?
opt1: To stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance: that ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and of the commandment of us the apostles of the Lord and Saviour
opt2: To compose an elaborate manual of ecclesiastical liturgy and ceremonial ordinances
opt3: To negotiate terms of political truce between believers and Roman imperial authorities
opt4: To settle jurisdictional disputes regarding episcopal authority among eastern provinces
correct: To stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance: that ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and of the commandment of us the apostles of the Lord and Saviour
explanation: Peter's overarching objective in both letters was to awaken and stimulate the believers' minds to retain the prophetic Scriptures and the authoritative commands of Christ's apostles. 2 Peter 3:1-2 (KJV) - "This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you; in both which I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance: That ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and of the commandment of us the apostles of the Lord and Saviour:"

question: What cynical uniformitarian objection will scoffers raise in the last days as they walk after their own lusts?
opt1: Why did the apostles fail to establish a visible military stronghold in Jerusalem?
opt2: Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation
opt3: Who authorized the preaching of the gospel to Gentile cities outside Judea?
opt4: How can any resurrection occur before the complete restoration of the temple walls?
correct: Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation
explanation: Scoffers will mock the promise of Christ's Second Advent by asserting an unbroken, unchanging continuum of natural history, rationalizing their carnal indulgence. 2 Peter 3:3-4 (KJV) - "Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation."

question: What historic divine intervention do scoffers willfully ignore, and what future destiny is reserved for the present heavens and earth?
opt1: That the ancient world perished through prolonged volcanic eruptions, and the present cosmos will freeze into eternal ice
opt2: That the antediluvian civilization collapsed through civil warfare, and the earth will be consumed by pestilence
opt3: That by the word of God the ancient world overflowed with water perished, but the heavens and the earth which are now are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment
opt4: That the earth was created without divine intervention, and will naturally evolve into perfection through human intellect
correct: That by the word of God the ancient world overflowed with water perished, but the heavens and the earth which are now are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment
explanation: Scoffers deliberately overlook that God once cataclysmically judged the world through the Flood, and that the same sovereign Word has reserved the present cosmos for universal destruction by fire. 2 Peter 3:5-7 (KJV) - "For this they willingly are ignorant of, that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water: Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished: But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men."

question: What essential divine perspective regarding time does Peter urge believers never to forget?
opt1: That the Lord measures time by the cyclical orbits of pagan astrological constellations
opt2: That each generation is granted precisely one millennium of physical longevity on earth
opt3: That divine decrees are subject to temporal revision every century by angelic councils
opt4: That one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day
correct: That one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day
explanation: God transcends human temporal limitations; an apparent delay from our mortal vantage point is merely a fleeting moment in the infinite perspective of the eternal Lord. 2 Peter 3:8 (KJV) - "But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day."

question: What is the true motivation behind the Lord's seeming delay in fulfilling His promise of return?
opt1: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance
opt2: The Lord has forgotten His covenant oath due to the widespread apostasy of the nations
opt3: The Lord is waiting until secular empires achieve universal economic stability and peace
opt4: The Lord is unable to execute judgment until angelic armies construct the heavenly city
correct: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance
explanation: Divine patience is not weakness, neglect, or indecision, but an expression of profound mercy, providing time for sinners to repent before final judgment arrives. 2 Peter 3:9 (KJV) - "The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance."

question: How does Peter describe the sudden arrival and cosmic impact of the Day of the Lord in 2 Peter 3:10?
opt1: The day of the Lord will arrive with scheduled trumpet convocations arranged by civil governors
opt2: The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up
opt3: The day of the Lord will bring an era of gradual political enlightenment where weapons turn to ploughshares
opt4: The day of the Lord will gently submerge the coastlines while preserving earthly monuments untouched
correct: The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up
explanation: The Day of the Lord will strike unexpectedly like a nocturnal thief, causing heavens to dissolve with a roaring crash, elements to melt with intense heat, and all earthly achievements to be consumed. 2 Peter 3:10 (KJV) - "But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up."

question: In light of the inevitable dissolution of the physical cosmos, what manner of life does Peter charge believers to cultivate?
opt1: In accumulating earthly treasures and landholdings to insulate against the final catastrophe
opt2: In engaging in political conspiracies to overthrow the persecuting magistrates of Rome
opt3: In all holy conversation and godliness, looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, looking for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness
opt4: In fatalistic despair and total withdrawal from all practical acts of brotherly love
correct: In all holy conversation and godliness, looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, looking for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness
explanation: Certainty of future cosmic dissolution demands intense moral purity and godliness, as saints anticipate God's promised new heavens and new earth characterized by absolute righteousness. 2 Peter 3:11-13 (KJV) - "Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness, Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat? Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness."

question: Seeing that believers look for such glorious new creations, what personal diligence does Peter urge in 2 Peter 3:14?
opt1: Be diligent that ye may amass large quantities of gold and silver against inflationary crisis
opt2: Be diligent that ye may debate every contentious genealogical riddle before magistrates
opt3: Be diligent that ye may achieve public applause and civic honors throughout Asia
opt4: Be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless
correct: Be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless
explanation: Eschatological hope requires moral diligence, challenging believers to live in spotless integrity and peace so that Christ finds them unblemished at His coming. 2 Peter 3:14 (KJV) - "Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless."

question: How does Peter endorse the inspired epistles of Paul, and what solemn warning does he give concerning their distortion by unstable men?
opt1: Our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction
opt2: Paul wrote human opinions without apostolic authority, which should be rejected by circumcision churches
opt3: Paul's epistles were written exclusively for Greek philosophers and contain no binding moral precepts
opt4: Paul retracted his theological teachings concerning grace when he visited Peter in Jerusalem
correct: Our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction
explanation: Peter explicitly affirms Paul's letters as divinely inspired Scripture, warning that ungrounded and unstable teachers twist their profound teachings, just as they do other Scriptures, to their own eternal ruin. 2 Peter 3:15-16 (KJV) - "And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction."

question: With what final apostolic caution, exhortation to growth, and doxology does Peter conclude his second epistle?
opt1: Beware of the legions of Caesar, and preserve your lives by fleeing into mountain fortresses. Amen.
opt2: Beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness: but grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen.
opt3: Beware of the rituals of the Gentiles, and reinstate the circumcision of Abraham in every assembly. Amen.
opt4: Beware of manual labor in this present age, and await the end in silent inactivity. Amen.
correct: Beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness: but grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen.
explanation: Peter closes with a vital double imperative: guarding against deception to prevent spiritual collapse, while actively growing in grace and the knowledge of Christ, to whom belongs eternal glory. 2 Peter 3:17-18 (KJV) - "Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness. But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and for ever. Amen."
